title: Step 60-F filters sorting and cursor pagination
description: Implement authoritative public listing filters, canonical sorting, cursor pagination, removable selections and history-safe URL state for Search and Category. Backend remains authoritative. Pricing and Inventory modules are read-only through their existing public ports; no write to those sensitive modules, no database migration and no frontend-invented pricing/availability semantics. Primary UX follows SF-B-05: availability, brand and Toman price range, plus route-appropriate sort; category-only attribute-value filters may render only from GET /categories/{slug}/filters. Advanced queries are evaluated on a bounded candidate set and fail closed rather than silently truncate. Stage 60-F may update only the CatalogQueryService mock fixture in test/catalog-search-step09.spec.ts so historical Step-09 assertions continue to exercise the same behavior after new read-only candidate/facet dependencies; Step-09 assertions themselves must remain semantically unchanged. Historical Storefront acceptance verifiers from Step59 and 60-C/D/E may be transitioned only where their frozen boundary explicitly prohibited filters/sort/pagination or their API fixtures predate mandatory ListingFacets/category-filter metadata. Their original Search/Category authority, recovery, SSR and later-step boundary assertions remain enforced. Provider Canonical CI #964 proved a historical Step56/57 provenance hash cascade is required after intentional OpenAPI/Catalog source changes. The authorized design files are source-hash/generated-audit reconciliation only; semantic design content is frozen.

evidence.design_recovery_cascade: Canonical CI #964 failed closed because Step56/57 provenance pins the intentionally changed OpenAPI/Catalog sources. Stage 60-F authorizes the same source-hash-only deterministic cascade used canonically in Step 60-B: refresh changed source SHA256 entries, propagate contract/manifest sourceSha256 values through Step56 B-G, regenerate deterministic Step56-H audit artifacts, and refresh Step57 source-linked hashes only as generator parity requires. No validator, screen/journey/operation semantics, reviewStatus, approval, runtime-release claim, Pricing/Inventory source, or historical transport evidence may change.

acceptance_criteria.description: Backend/OpenAPI support canonical public listing query keys. Category supports brand, min_price, max_price, available, sort and category-authoritative attribute_value selections; Search supports brand, min_price, max_price, available and route-appropriate sort. Unsupported or malformed values fail closed before result fabrication.

Pricing and stock filtering/sorting use existing PricingPublicPort and InventoryAvailabilityPort batch reads only. No Pricing/Inventory implementation files are changed and Catalog never reimplements effective price or online-sellable formulas.

Advanced filtering is complete over a bounded candidate set. If the safety bound would be exceeded, the request fails closed; it never silently truncates. Cursor is opaque, <=1024 bytes, bound to query/filter/sort fingerprint and stable ordering keys.

SF-B-05 primary controls are implemented: sort, in-stock-only, brand, Toman min/max, apply/clear, removable selections, status summary and history-safe next-page cursor. Applying/removing any result-set dimension resets cursor. Search preserves q; Category preserves slug. Category attribute controls are generated only from authoritative category filter metadata.

Search default remains backend relevance; Category default remains newest. No client-side re-ranking occurs. Toman is integer-only, Wallet is absent, brown remains prohibited and logical RTL/touch-target contracts are preserved.

Canonical completion requires exact-head root verify, Phase A, Storefront quality, deterministic Review, exact-artifact Lock, protected merge, exact-SHA postmerge verification and terminal Lock release before 60-G.

external_gate_evidence.rule: Risk is declared MEDIUM because sensitive Pricing/Inventory write paths are explicitly forbidden. Provider risk classification is authoritative; any HIGH classification requires Security + Owner Human Gate before merge.
